rules.F (extended): The wait a FENCE-class instruction imposes on its warp is booked on the first instance behind it (at most 16 ahead) whose control word's wait mask contains the FENCE's write barrier; none: on the next instance to issue. This holds for both forms the engine has of that wait: the suspended:descriptor_visibility interval (version 1 addendum) and the part of a control:fence:<class> interval beyond the FENCE's stall field (rule M's name; the stall-field part stays control_floor on the next instance). Intervals named control:membar are unchanged (booked on the next instance).

addenda.when: 2026-11-20, cause of the 37 full-GPU failures of rule P found (case cublas_bf16_skinny_00, kept jobs and journals in $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/pdiag/{new,old}: new = build 47eaf2ff with P, old = build 3b5718c2)
addenda.text: Segment 9, mbarrier object 1: with P a second arrive at cycle 11801 while the first phase is open (overrun); without P the next arrive comes at 20516. The arriving warp (224) issues its waits on other objects one cycle after the poll with P (journal: instance 378528 at cycle 10806, wait 0) where without P the same wait holds it 2446 cycles (instance 378463 at 13252). Job dump of that wait (segment 9): without P the surviving poll is the final ready out-of-line TRYWAIT (write barrier 0, wait mask 0x4) and the BRA behind it has wait mask 0x1: it waits for the poll's pending result. With P the surviving poll is the first, inline TRYWAIT (write barrier 2, mbarrier_wait flags 0x1, after_ready 0xffffffff) and the instructions kept behind it are the tail of the last attempt (NANOSLEEP.SYNCS wait mask 0x1, predicated-off PHASECHK, BRA wait mask 0x1, MOV 0x2): none has barrier 2 in its wait mask, and the instruction that had (the out-of-line TRYWAIT, wait mask 0x4, the inline poll's reader in this layout) is a poll of the folded run and was dropped. The pending result of the surviving poll therefore holds nobody; every such wait is passed at once, producers overrun their barriers (mbarrier_overrun) or consumers run ahead into a deadlock. The probes passed because in u.pollcute and u.handoff_hint the first poll's reader is not itself a poll and is kept. So P's defect is in the rule: moving the surviving instance to another static instruction severs the dependency-barrier link between the poll and the stream behind it whenever the kept records and the first poll do not share a barrier. A rule that leaves the converted stream alone and moves only the booking cannot do this: protocol v4.
